purpose: Normalize source identity, textual lineage, author/school grouping, and evidence independence for future LiuYao rule registration without changing current-22 runtime behavior.
principles: A source title is not automatically an independent evidence vote.
Textual transmission, quotation, commentary, and shared-formula relationships must be recorded at evidence scope when they affect independence.
Multiple works by the same modern author are separate witnesses but not automatically independent author/school votes.
Source independence and proposition compatibility are different concepts.
Research may finish with conflicted or insufficient evidence; provenance normalization must not force consensus.
Current frozen rules retain their existing runtime tiers until a separately reviewed migration is performed.

evidenceSpecificOverrideRequiredWhen: a compilation contains both transmitted material and genuinely separate chapters
two sources share only a bounded formula or passage rather than the whole work
a modern author changes or refines a rule across different works

futureConsensusRules.stableConsensusMinimum: Must be justified from reviewed independent evidence groups, not raw sourceRef count; no universal numeric threshold is imposed by this v0.1 registry.
futureConsensusRules.modernConsensusMinimum: Must include more than one independent modern author/school group when the proposition is claimed as modern cross-author consensus.
futureConsensusRules.singleAuthorMultipleWorks: May strengthen internal consistency or show refinement, but remains one modern author/school group for independence counting.
futureConsensusRules.conflictHandling: Conflicting independent groups must remain visible; do not average them into a synthetic consensus label.

migrationNotes: The existing js/liuyao-rule-registry.js embeds SOURCES and EVIDENCES and currently labels some evidence classical_multi_source or modern_consensus without normalized lineage metadata.
This v0.1 file does not alter those current-22 runtime labels because that would mutate frozen behavior.
All future next-topic evidence IDs should reference this normalized registry or a reviewed successor before formal Rule Registry promotion.
A future current-22 provenance migration, if desired, must be separately versioned and regression-tested.
